name: Modal Dialog
description: An accessible modal dialog for confirmations and short tasks, built on the project's dialog component or native <dialog>: focus moves in and comes back, Escape and backdrop rules, a busy state that survives a failed action, a page that stays still behind it, and a full-screen layout on phones.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing dialogs win.

layout.layering: Native <dialog> opened with showModal() is drawn in the top layer and needs no z-index. Without it, the backdrop and the dialog sit above every other layer the project defines: page content, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, and toasts.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Add a modal dialog for confirmations and short tasks without leaving the page. Build on the project's dialog component when it has a suitable one; otherwise use native <dialog> opened with showModal(). Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: Built on the project's dialog component, or native <dialog> opened with showModal(), which draws it in the top layer and makes the rest of the page inert
Named by its visible title; a short plain-text message can describe it
Focus moves in on open (to Cancel in confirmations) and returns on close, or to a sensible place nearby when the trigger is gone
Closes with Escape, a visible Cancel or Close button, and optionally a backdrop click that ignores text selections dragged out of the dialog
A busy primary action keeps focus and has a time limit, and a failure keeps the dialog open with the error inside it
The page behind it doesn't scroll or shift
Centered up to 640 px wide; full screen or near-full width on phones, sized with dvh
Optional short motion, and no movement under reduced motion
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has a dialog or modal component, configure or extend it to meet this guide instead of building another one, and keep its API.
2. Choose what the task needs: the variant (dialog or alertdialog), whether Escape closes it, whether a backdrop click closes it, and whether it goes full screen on phones. Leave out the rest.

3. Without a suitable component, use native <dialog> and open it with showModal(), as in frameworkPatterns.nativeDialog. Don't use the open attribute or show() for a modal: they give a non-modal dialog without a backdrop or an inert page.
4. Wire opening, focus, and every way of closing as in componentSpec.interactions.
5. Add the primary action's busy, success, and failure states (componentSpec.interactions and edgeCases.busyClose).
6. Lock page scrolling (implementationDetails.pageScrollLock), add the layouts in componentSpec.responsiveBehavior, then the optional motion in animations.
7. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, and a touch device, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

componentSpec.goal: Provide a safe, accessible modal dialog for confirmations, forms, and focused tasks without leaving the current page context.

anatomy.hierarchy: The trigger opens the dialog. The dialog holds the title, an optional close button, an optional short description, the body, the status message, and the actions. The backdrop covers the page; native <dialog> draws it as ::backdrop.

slotNotes.title: A visible heading that names the dialog through aria-labelledby.
slotNotes.description: Optional: one short plain-text message, as in a confirmation, referenced by aria-describedby. Leave it out when the body holds a form or longer content, which a screen reader would read in full on open.
slotNotes.body: The content. It scrolls inside the dialog when it is long.
slotNotes.statusMessage: An element with role="status", present from the moment the dialog opens, for busy and error text.
slotNotes.actions: Cancel and the primary action, named for what it does ("Delete project", not "OK").
slotNotes.closeButton: Optional icon button with an accessible name such as "Close". Every dialog has a visible Cancel or Close button, because touch and screen reader users may have no Escape key.

open.description: Whether the dialog is shown as a modal.

loading.description: Whether the primary action is running; see the primaryActionClick interaction.

variant.description: dialog for most uses; alertdialog for an urgent decision, such as confirming a deletion.

dismissible.description: Whether Escape, or the back gesture on Android, closes the dialog.

closeOnBackdropClick.description: Whether a click on the backdrop closes a dismissible dialog. Turn it off for alert dialogs and for forms with typed input.

fullscreenOnMobile.description: Whether the dialog fills the screen below the mobile breakpoint.

interactions.accessibilityNotes: Initial focus goes to the least destructive action (usually Cancel) in confirmations and alert dialogs, to the first field in a form, and to the title or the top of the content (tabindex="-1") when the content is long or should be read first; otherwise to the first focusable element. With native <dialog>, put autofocus on that element.

Escape, and the back gesture on Android, sends a close request: native <dialog> fires cancel, then close. When the dialog isn't dismissible or is busy, call preventDefault() on cancel. Browsers may still close it on a repeated request without other user interaction, so treat every close as the safe choice, Cancel, never as a confirmation.

Count a click only when the press also started on the backdrop: a text selection dragged from inside the dialog onto the backdrop ends in a click on the dialog, and must not close it. With native <dialog>, give the dialog no padding of its own, so only a backdrop click targets the <dialog> element. Where supported, closedby="any" does this natively; keep the script for other browsers.
While the primary action runs, Cancel and Close abort it if it can be aborted; otherwise they do nothing until it finishes.

Focus stays on the button: use aria-disabled="true" and ignore activation instead of the disabled attribute, which drops focus to the page. Give the request a time limit (edgeCases.stuckOperation). A form dialog validates first; on errors it stays open and moves focus to the first invalid field.
The status message shows the error, so it's announced, and focus stays on the primary action, so the user can retry or cancel. Running out of time is a failure too, with a message that says so.

Every way of closing ends here. Focus returns to the trigger; native <dialog> does this itself. If the trigger is gone (Delete removed its row), move focus to a sensible place nearby, such as the next item, the list, or its heading (tabindex="-1"), never to the page body. If the list updates only after the dialog has closed, move focus when it updates.

mobile.behavior: With fullscreenOnMobile, the dialog fills the screen: 100vw wide (100% would leave a reserved scrollbar gutter uncovered), 100dvh tall (100vh as the fallback), no margins or rounded corners, and padding that includes the safe-area insets. Otherwise it's near-full width with 16 px gutters and at most calc(100dvh - 64px) tall.

tabletAndDesktop.behavior: Centered, at most 640 px wide and calc(100dvh - 64px) tall. The title row and the actions stay visible while the body scrolls.

shortViewport.behavior: On landscape phones and at high zoom, the whole content scrolls, actions included, instead of keeping the title row and actions in place.

responsiveBehavior.reflow: At 320 px wide, which is 400% zoom on a 1280 px screen, nothing scrolls sideways.
responsiveBehavior.nativeDefaults: The browser stylesheet gives dialog:modal default margins and maximum sizes; override them for the full-screen layout.

variants.confirm: A question, a short explanation, Cancel, and the confirming action named for what it does. Initial focus on Cancel.
variants.alert: role="alertdialog" for an urgent decision, such as deleting something. The short message is its description, and a backdrop click doesn't close it.
variants.form: Fields in the body and a submit action. A backdrop click doesn't close it, so a stray click can't lose typed input, and validation follows the project's form rules. Optional: ask before discarding typed input.
variants.progress: Shows an operation in progress. Its Cancel aborts the operation; if the operation can't be cancelled, an error with Retry and Close appears after a timeout, so nobody is stuck.
variants.fullscreen: Full screen at every width, for long forms or content that needs the space.

animations.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing moves: a short fade, or no animation.
animations.nativeDialog: Animate the open with @starting-style. Animating the close also needs transition-behavior: allow-discrete on display and overlay; where a browser can't do that, the dialog closes at once, which is fine. Focus returns and the page unlocks at once, not after the animation.

requirements.1.3.1: The title is a heading, and it names the dialog (aria-labelledby).
requirements.1.4.10: At 320 px wide the dialog fits without horizontal scrolling.
requirements.1.4.11: Focus indicators and control boundaries have at least 3:1 contrast.
requirements.2.1.1: Every control works from the keyboard. A scrolling body without focusable content is focusable itself (tabindex="0") and named.
requirements.2.1.2: The dialog can always be left: Escape when it's dismissible, and its Cancel or Close button (componentSpec.anatomy.slotNotes.closeButton).
requirements.2.4.3: Focus moves into the dialog on open and returns on close (componentSpec.interactions).
requirements.2.4.7: Every control shows a visible focus indicator.
requirements.2.5.8: The close button and the actions are at least 24 by 24 CSS px.
requirements.4.1.2: role dialog or alertdialog, modal, and named by its title.
requirements.4.1.3: Busy and error messages are announced through the status message without moving focus.

keyboardNavigation.tab: Tab and Shift+Tab move through the dialog's controls. With native <dialog>, focus can also reach the browser's own controls, but never the page behind.
keyboardNavigation.enter: In a form dialog, Enter submits the form as usual.

dialog.aria-labelledby: The id of the visible title
dialog.role: alertdialog for the alert variant; native <dialog> is already a dialog
dialog.aria-modal: true, but only on a dialog that isn't native <dialog> opened with showModal()

closeButton.name: An accessible name such as "Close", from visually hidden text or aria-label

dialog.aria-describedby: The id of a short plain-text message; see componentSpec.anatomy.slotNotes.description

trigger.aria-haspopup: "dialog", if screen readers should say the button opens a dialog. Never "true", which announces a menu.
trigger.aria-expanded: Rarely useful for a modal; the WAI-ARIA APG modal dialog example uses neither attribute.

statusMessage.usage: Present from the moment the dialog opens; holds the busy and error text.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

nativeDialog.description: A delete confirmation in plain HTML and JavaScript; adapt it to the project's framework and its version. It covers the parts that are easy to get wrong: the backdrop check, the cancel event, the busy state and its time limit, results that arrive after the dialog closed, and focus when the trigger is gone. deleteProject() and notify() stand for the app's own request and its toast or page message.
nativeDialog.html:
Delete project?

This deletes the project and its files for everyone on the team.

plainCss.description: Plain CSS for the parts the browser doesn't provide. Use the project's styling system and tokens instead of these values.

implementationDetails.pageScrollLock: Native <dialog> and inert stop clicks and focus behind the dialog, but not scrolling. Set overflow: hidden on the root element while a modal is open (html:has(dialog:modal)), keep the scrollbar's space (scrollbar-gutter: stable on the root, or padding equal to the scrollbar's width while locked), and give the dialog's scrolling body overscroll-behavior: contain. iOS Safari can still scroll the page under a touch; where it does, fix the body in place while the dialog is open (position: fixed, with top set to minus the scroll position) and restore the scroll position on close.
implementationDetails.formDialogs: <form method="dialog"> closes the dialog on submit and sets returnValue to the submit button's value, which is enough for confirmations without async work. A form that saves data handles submit itself, as the primary action does.
implementationDetails.withoutNativeDialog: Only when neither the project nor native <dialog> fits, for example an overlay system the project must keep: render the dialog at the end of body with role="dialog" (or "alertdialog") and aria-modal="true"; make every sibling of its container inert while it's open, which keeps focus in the dialog without a focus-trap library; move focus in and return it as in componentSpec.interactions; close on Escape with a keydown listener on the dialog; give the backdrop element the same press-and-click check; and put the backdrop and the dialog at the top of the project's layering scale. Don't hide the page with aria-hidden instead of inert.

edgeCases.busyClose: While the primary action runs, Escape and backdrop clicks do nothing. Cancel and Close abort it only when aborting really stops the work, such as an upload or a search; a request that changes data can still finish on the server, so for that they wait. If the browser closes the dialog anyway, for example after a repeated Escape or back gesture, show the result in the page, for example in a toast, and if focus was lost with the trigger, move it as in the dialogClosed interaction. Opened again before the result arrives, the dialog shows the busy state again.
edgeCases.stuckOperation: Give the request a time limit the project picks, for example 30 seconds (AbortSignal.timeout() with fetch). When it runs out, show an error that says so and make the actions work again, so the person can retry or cancel. Tell a timeout from other failures by the signal's reason (signal.reason.name is "TimeoutError"), not by the error: WebKit rejects fetch with an AbortError.
edgeCases.stackedDialogs: Avoid a dialog on top of a dialog; replace the content instead. When it can't be avoided, showModal() stacks it: Escape closes the top one, and focus returns into the one below. Without native <dialog>, make the lower dialog inert too.
edgeCases.toasts: A toast below an open modal can't be reached. Show the result of the dialog's action after it closes, or inside the dialog while it stays open.
edgeCases.longContent: The body scrolls inside the dialog (overflow: auto, overscroll-behavior: contain) while the title row and actions stay visible. If it holds no focusable element, make it focusable (tabindex="0") and name it, so keyboard users can scroll it.
edgeCases.rapidToggle: Ignore the trigger while the dialog opens or closes, so a double click never opens two.
edgeCases.navigation: If the route changes while the dialog is open, close it without returning focus to a trigger on the old page.
edgeCases.serverRendering: Render the dialog closed, and call showModal() only in the browser, after mount.

must: Build on the project's dialog component when it has a suitable one, and keep its API
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
Implement only the options and variants the task needs
Give every dialog a visible Cancel or Close button
Return focus on every way of closing, including when the trigger is gone
mustNot: Add a dependency, such as a focus-trap, scroll-lock, or UI library, without asking
Show a modal with the open attribute or show(); use showModal()
Hide the page with aria-hidden instead of a native modal or inert
Close on a click that started inside the dialog
Put the disabled attribute on the focused action while it's busy
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: Opened from the keyboard, focus lands as the initial-focus rule says, and a screen reader announces the dialog's role and title, plus its short description if it has one
Tab and Shift+Tab never reach the page behind it, and the page can't be clicked or scrolled, including by touch on iOS Safari
Opening it doesn't shift the page's layout
Escape closes a dismissible dialog, and focus returns to the trigger; a dialog that isn't dismissible stays open on the first Escape, and any close counts as Cancel
A backdrop click closes the dialog only when that's turned on, and dragging a text selection from inside onto the backdrop never closes it
Every dialog has a visible Cancel or Close button with an accessible name, at least 24 by 24 px

While the primary action runs, focus stays on its button and the status message announces progress; a failure keeps the dialog open with the error announced and the buttons working; a success closes it
A request that never settles ends at its time limit with an error and working buttons, and a result that arrives after the dialog closed shows in the page without leaving focus on the page body
When the action removed the trigger, focus lands in a sensible place nearby, not on the page body
At 320 px wide and at 400% zoom nothing scrolls sideways and the actions stay reachable; on phones, the full-screen dialog isn't hidden behind the browser's toolbars
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens, like its other components

relatedPotions.description: Optional: toasts sit below an open modal, so show an action result after the dialog closes, or inside it while it stays open.
